name: PCBP2 condensates
description: The PCBP2 condensate is a biomolecular condensate formed as a result of phase separation of poly(C)-binding protein 2 (PCBP2). PCBP2 condensates sequester mitochondrial and mRNA-binding proteins, leading to the outside impairment of mitochondrial morphology and function, and BACE1 mRNA decay relative to amyloid deposition. Mitochondrial proteins sequestered by PCBP2 are not found in reported processing bodies (PB) or stress granules (SG).

name: CEBPZ condensates

name: c‐Maf condensates
description: The c-Maf condensate is a biomolecular condensate formed as a result of phase separation of the transcription factor c-Maf. Alanine‐rich intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) in c‐Maf drive hydrophobic interactions, enabling phase separation. c‐Maf recruits RNA Polymerase II via phase separation to establish transcriptional condensates that upregulate Mtbp transcription.

name: Stress granule
description: Stress granules (SGs) are condensed membrane-less organelles that form dynamically as RNA and protein (RNP) phase separate during physiological stress. When translation initiation is limited, SGs assemble and play a role in translational regulation and proteome buffering. Translationally stalled mRNAs, translation initiation factors, RNA-binding proteins, and non-RNA-binding proteins are among the constituents of SGs. SGs are one of the most important cellular stress relievers, yet their presence are temporary. Any condition that causes permanent presence of SGs, such as chronic stress or alterations in the structure of the components of SGs, can induce their pathological aggregation and degenerative effects.

name: Mast cell extracellular granules (MCEGs)
description: Mast cell extracellular granules (MCEGs) are condensates found in the extracellular space, assembled through electrostatic interactions between glycosaminoglycans and polyamines.

name: α-synuclein condensates
description: In human cell models, stressors could promote the abnormal phase separation of α-synuclein, leading to the formation of solid-like, pathological aggregates. This process is linked to cellular stress, including the unfolded protein response, and is considered a key step preceding aggregation in neurodegenerative diseases. In C. elegans models expressing human α-synuclein, the environmental pollutant PHCZ accelerates the formation of α-synuclein condensates and reduces their fluidity, promoting a pathological solid-like state.

name: EWSR1 condensates

name: Plectin condensates

name: Transcriptional condensate
description: Transcriptional condensates are bimolecular condensates which form by phase separation of transcription factors, mediator cofactors and numerous nucleic-acid binding proteins at enhancer sites of gene loci, promoting bimolecular interactions which are necessary for gene expression.

name: Cajal body
description: Cajal bodies are nuclear bodies which are composed of the scaffolding protein  Coilin and high concentrations of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) which are involved in pre-mRNA splicing.These condensates are also suggested to contribute to RNA metabolism including snRNP biogenesis and telomerase biogenesis.

name: INAVA condensates
description: INAVA condensates are membraneless compartments formed via phase separation in response to cellular stressors-such as reactive oxygen species or proteasome inhibitors-to regulate protein ubiquitination and degradation.

name: GAS2L3 condensates

name: AFAP1-AS1 condensates
description: The AFAP1-AS1 condensate is a biomolecular condensate formed as a result of phase separation of the long non-coding RNA actin filament associated protein 1 antisense RNA 1 (AFAP1-AS1). name: DNA damage foci
description: Double-strand breaks can be caused by a variety of physical and chemical factors, such as ionizing radiation and radiomimetic medicines, but they can also develop as secondary lesions during replication and DNA repair after exposure to a variety of genotoxins. Repair proteins aggregate at damaged areas in response to double strand breaks (DSB), forming membrane-less  subnuclear foci, supporting DNA repair. Rad52 DNA repair proteins assemble in liquid droplets at distinct DNA damage sites, which then fuse into a repair centre droplet.  Together with the repair centre droplet, Rad52 concentrates tubulin and projects short aster-like DIMs (aster-DIMs), which connect the repair center to longer DIMs, allowing damaged DNA to be mobilized to the nuclear periphery for repair. Collaboration between Rad52 liquid droplets and different types of nuclear filaments aids in the formation and function of the DNA repair centre.

name: BAG2
description: BAG2 condensates are found in the cytosol and triggered by several forms of stress, particularly hyper-osmotic stress. These condensates facilitate client degradation through the 20S proteasome, independent of ubiquitin. Unlike most condensates, BAG2 condensates do not contain RNA. These structures safeguard cell viability during stress and can move towards the client protein. Inhibition of the proteasome leads to the relocation of BAG2 condensates and autophagy markers to an aggresome-like structure.

name: Granular component
description: Granular component (GC) is one of the three substructures of the nucleolus. GC is the site where final maturation of the pre-ribosomal ribonucleoprotein and assembly with ribosomal proteins occur, after their transcription either in the fibrillar centres (FCs) or at the boundary between the FC and the dense fibrillar component (DFC) region.

name: Sup35 condensate
description: When yeast is under stress, Sup35 creates protective gels through pH-controlled liquid-like phase separation and gelation. Phase separation in this instance is facilitated by the N-terminal prion domain and controlled by the nearby pH sensor domain. The Sup35 translation factor is through this process protected from stress-related damage by phase separation, which aids in yeast survival

name: Neuronal RNP granule
description: Neuronal RNP granules are nonmembrane bound macromolecular condensates that concentrate certain sets of mRNAs and regulatory proteins, allowing them to travel longer distances to axons or dendrites. RNP granules in neurons have a dual role in regulating the translation of linked mRNAs: at rest, they impede mRNA translation, but once activated, they fuel local protein synthesis.

name: SPOP/DAXX body

SPOP and DAXX are suggested to interact with each other and together they colocalize at distinct spots in the nucleus and form  a different, largely spherical type of nuclear body distinct from nuclear speckles, PML bodies, nucleoli, and Cajal bodies; named SPOP/DAXX bodies. Mutations which disrupt the interaction between SPOP and DAXX localizes SPOP to nuclear speckles and DAXX to the PML bodies.

name: cGAS foci
description: The cytosolic DNA sensor cGMP-AMP (cGAMP) synthase (cGAS) detects both pathogenic and mislocalized DNA in the cytoplasm and activates innate immunity. The immunological response to cancer and pathogen infection is dependent on cGAS detection of cytosolic DNA. The spatial limitation of the DNA sensor cGAS prevents abnormal intracellular detection of self-DNA. The development of cytoplasmic foci containing cGAS and DNA is triggered by DNA emerging in the cytoplasm. Human cGAS (h-cGAS) constitutes an important therapeutic target for modulation of antiinflammatory responses that can contribute to the emergence of autoimmune disorders.

description: TIFA undergoes liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) induced by ALPK1 in response to adenosine diphosphate (ADP)-β-D-manno-heptose (ADP-Hep) recognition. The phase separation of TIFA is primarily driven by ALPK1, the pT9-FHA domain, and the intrinsically disordered region segment. Simultaneously, TRAF6 exhibits phase separation during ADP-Hep-induced inflammation, a phenomenon observed consistently across various inflammatory signal pathways.

name: PML body
description: PML bodies are nuclear condensates detected by the PML protein, as their name suggests. The PML protein polymerizes into spherical shells where it concentrates several unrelated partner proteins into the PML bodies. PML is found in nearly all normal human tissues and produces PML bodies, which play a role in gene regulation and cellular activities like DNA repair, cell cycle control, and cell fate decisions.

name: Nuclear pore complex
description: Nucleocytoplasmic exchange is mediated by nuclear pore complexes (NPCs). They're massive protein complexes that join the inner and outer nuclear membranes to create channels that span the nuclear envelope. Nucleoporins, which are made up of about 30 different protein components, assemble in many copies to form a complicated cylindrical architecture to the nuclear pores.

name: Heterochromatin
description: Chromatin is a complex of DNA and histone proteins that regulates gene expression as well as packaging genetic material to fit inside the cell. The proper functioning of chromatin also necessitates a web of interactions between molecular complexes that alter chromatin shape and organization to change DNA accessibility to transcription factors, resulting in the activation or repression of target DNA locus. Chromatin is divided into three types based on its shape and compaction state: euchromatin, heterochromatin, and centromeric chromatin. Heterochromatin is related with gene silencing and is characterized by being less accessible than euchromatin and transcriptionally less active. In the nucleus, heterochromatin separates from euchromatin and is concentrated in the nuclear periphery and regions around the nucleolus.

name: Carboxysome
description: Carboxysome is a bacterial organelle that has properties of a biomolecular condensate. Rubisco condensates formation is proposed to optimize the process of photosynthetic carbon fixation.

name: Htt inclusion
description: Inclusion bodies are insoluble aggregates of misfolded proteins inside the cell. A common pathogenic event in a range of neurodegenerative illnesses is aggregated proteins from the cytoplasm of nerve cells and glia. Misfolding and aggregation of huntingtin (Htt) protein results in Huntington's disease (HD), which is the most prevalent inherited neurodegenerative disease. The HD mutation causes an excessively long polyglutamine (polyQ) expansion in the Htt, which makes the protein more prone to aggregate.

name: VRN1 nuclear body

The nucleolus is responsible for ribosome biogenesis in eucaryotic cells, which are essential macromolecular machines responsible for synthesizing all proteins required by the cell. name: Nucleolus
description: Nucleolus is the largest and the first membrane-less organelle which was identified. It is composed of a fibrillar centre (FC), dense fibrillar component (DFC) and granular component (GC).  The nucleolus is a dynamic structure that disassembles during mitosis and reassembles after cell division. The nucleolus is responsible for ribosome biogenesis in eucaryotic cells, which are essential macromolecular machines responsible for synthesizing all proteins required by the cell. The nucleoli are now known to act as sensors and regulators of cellular responses, such as apoptosis, DNA damage response, epigenetic modification, genome stability, proliferation, senescence and signal transduction.

name: WNK body
description: WNK bodies are large distinct foci which form in the distal convoluted tubule (DCT) as the result of potassium imbalance. WNK body formation is dependent on kidney-specific WNK1 (KS-WNK1), a truncated kinase-defective WNK1 isoform that is strongly expressed in the DCT.

description: Cauliflower Mosaic Virus  forms inclusion bodies during infection, which are mostly made of the viral protein P6 and are the sites of viral activity.

name: ParABS DNA
description: ParABS DNA condensate is formed by the key component of the ParABS system, the ParB (spo0J) protein, which assembles dynamically on the DNA

name: Heterochromatin
description: Chromatin is a complex of DNA and histone proteins that regulates gene expression as well as packaging genetic material to fit inside the cell. The proper functioning of chromatin also necessitates a web of interactions between molecular complexes that alter chromatin shape and organization to change DNA accessibility to transcription factors, resulting in the activation or repression of target DNA locus. Chromatin is divided into three types based on its shape and compaction state: euchromatin, heterochromatin, and centromeric chromatin. Heterochromatin is related with gene silencing and is characterized by being less accessible than euchromatin and transcriptionally less active. In the nucleus, heterochromatin separates from euchromatin and is concentrated in the nuclear periphery and regions around the nucleolus.

name: GW-body
description: The mammalian analog of P-bodies is known as GW bodies. These are cytoplasmic foci involved in the breakdown of mRNA. RNA interference has been connected to GWBs in recent research, with disruption or disassembly of GWBs being shown to affect siRNA and miRNA silencing activity.

name: Virus-induced replication (VIR) condensate
description: The VIR-condensate is a condensate formed within viral replication organelles (VROs) during the replication of positive-strand RNA viruses. It is driven by phase separation of viral replication proteins and incorporates co-opted host proteins to create a dynamic microenvironment that facilitates efficient viral synthesis.

name: P-granule
description: P-granules are germ granules in C. elegans. P-granules are composed of a heterogenous mixture of RNAs and proteins. P-granule components are linked to RNA metabolism, implying their role in posttranscriptional control.

name: Galectin complex
description: The N-terminal domain of Galectin-3 contains aromatic residues which interact to phase separate the domain. This process is important for the extracellular agglutination function of Galectin-3.

name: Pericentriolar matrix
description: Cetrosomes are the main microtubule organising centers (MTOC) of animal cells and thus are critical in regulating cell-cycle progression. Centrosomes nucleate microtubules during mitosis, allowing for chromosomal segregation. Each centrosome contains 2 centrioles arranged perpendicularly and surrounded by pericentriolar material (PCM).

name: FXR1 condensates
description: FXR1 undergoes phase separation to form mRNP granules in Late Spermatids (LS) and are indispensable for the male fertility in mice. FXR1 recruits translation factors like ELF4G3 into the condensates. The fusion of these FXR1 condensates with RNP granules in germ cells activate the translation of the stored mRNA .

name: Yb-body
description: Yb-bodies are perinuclear foci in Drosophila ovarian somatic cells, which  are thought to be the site of PIWI interacting RNA (piRNA) synthesis (OSCs). Yb bodies are multivalent condensates that are formed by Yb-Yb homotypic interaction and   interaction with flamenco RNA transcripts, which are the source of transposon-repressing piRNAs.

name: Presynaptic clusters
description: Presynaptic clusters are clusters of synaptic vesicles at presynaptic sites.  Synapsin is the abundant protein associated with synaptic vesicles condensates.

name: SMN1 nuclear body
description: Nuclear bodies are membraneless, RNA-rich organelles in the cell nucleus that concentrate certain nuclear proteins and RNA-protein complexes.

name: Stress granule
description: Stress granules (SGs) are condensed membrane-less organelles that form dynamically as RNA and protein (RNP) phase separate during physiological stress. Translationally stalled mRNAs, translation initiation factors, RNA-binding proteins, and non-RNA-binding proteins are among the constituents of SGs. SGs are one of the most important cellular stress relievers, yet their presence are temporary. Any condition that causes permanent presence of SGs, such as chronic stress or alterations in the structure of the components of SGs, can induce their pathological aggregation and degenerative effects.

name: Ede1 condensate
description: Ede1 is an endocytic  protein. Excess Ede1 in yeast cells phase separates into large condensates which  are able recruit other endocytic proteins.

name: Transcriptional condensate
description: Transcriptional condensates are bimolecular condensates which form by phase separation of transcription factors, mediator cofactors and numerous nucleic-acid binding proteins at enhancer sites of gene loci, promoting bimolecular interactions which are necessary for gene expression.

name: Elastin granule
description: Monomers in elastin can phase separate and self-assemble into polymer networks with elasticity and robustness.

description: Morphology: In Vivo Droplet Formation; Main protein: Q13535; Partner Proteins: Q92547, Q99638; On fluorescence microscopy, optogenetic TopBP1 condensates co-localized with RAD9 and with phospho ATR.

name: Stress granule
description:
Trypanosoma brucei

Stress granules in the unicellular protest and parasite Trypanosoma brucei form under heat shock and puromycin treatment, upon polysome disassembly, at the periphery of the cell and are distinct from P-bodies.

name: CCR4-NOT1 complex
description: CCR4-NOT1 complex plays an important role in mRNA deanylation.

name: Nuclear pore complex
description: Nucleocytoplasmic exchange is mediated by nuclear pore complexes (NPCs). They're massive protein complexes that join the inner and outer nuclear membranes to create channels that span the nuclear envelope. Nucleoporins, which are made up of about 30 different protein components, assemble in many copies to form a complicated cylindrical architecture to the nuclear pores.

name: DDX1 body
description: DDX1 body is a type of nuclear bodies. DDX1 bodies contain the protein DEAD box DDX1 protein, which  is a potential RNA unwinding protein linked to RNA processing and transport. Cleavage bodies and DDX1 bodies are frequently found colocalizing in the nucleus.

name: Negri body
description: Negri bodies (NBs) are inclusions or viral factories in the cytoplasm of the host cell where rabies virus replicates.

name: P-body
description: P-bodies are cytosolic biomolecular condensates that arise in response to environmental stress when translationally-arrested mRNAs and proteins phase separate at specific regions in the cytoplasm. In this way, P-bodies are important for translation regulation and proteome buffering.
